title: PowerToys does not start automatically on boot
author: Hydrooxzgen

status.label: Likely duplicate of existing startup tracker
status.detail: The report matches the open PowerToys startup failure tracker #23193; earlier similar reports #43395, #41683, and #36993 were already consolidated there.

next_action.label: Post duplicate-routing comment
next_action.reason: The author supplied a PowerToysReport ZIP after the automated triage request, but the core symptom is already tracked publicly in #23193.

judgment.rationale: Issue 50379 is a clear current report of the same General PowerToys auto-start failure already tracked by open issue #23193. Prior duplicates #43395, #41683, and #36993 were closed into that chain, and no linked upstream PR or separate owner was found for 50379. Keeping this report linked to #23193 avoids parallel triage while preserving the newly supplied diagnostic attachment as supporting evidence.
evidence: Issue 50379 reports PowerToys 0.101.2362 Stable from GitHub on Windows 11 25H2, system installation, running as admin, with Run at startup enabled but PowerToys not launching after reboot.
The reporter attached multiple PowerToysReport ZIP links and then replied that the report file was added after automated triage asked for a fresh report.
The issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Product-General, Needs-Triage, Needs-Author-Feedback, and Needs-Team-Response, with no assignee or project item.

Issue #43395 describes PowerToys not automatically running after logon; it was closed as duplicate of #41683, which was closed as duplicate of #36993, which was closed as duplicate of open issue #23193.
Open issue #23193 tracks the same broad behavior: PowerToys does not run at startup even when the setting is enabled, including reports while running as administrator and after updates.
No public PR referencing #50379, #43395, #41683, #36993, or #23193 was found during the lightweight refresh.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a maintainer-ready comment routing this report to #23193 as the existing tracker, then close as duplicate if maintainers agree.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix is plausible for the startup-task path, but this specific issue should not start a separate fix workflow because an open upstream tracker (#23193) already covers the same failure family and contains broader historical diagnostics. Treat 50379 as duplicate/handled rather than proposing a competing design from this child issue.

issue_context.summary: A Windows 11 25H2 user reports that PowerToys 0.101.2362 does not start after reboot even though General > Run at startup is enabled. The reporter supplied PowerToysReport ZIP attachments after automated triage initially noted that diagnostics were unavailable or rejected, and the remaining decision is whether to route the report into the existing startup failure tracker.
known_information: PowerToys version is 0.101.2362 Stable, installed from GitHub.
The reporter is on Windows 11 25H2 / 10.0.101, Simplified Chinese, system installation, and says PowerToys is running as admin.
Reproduction steps are: open General settings, enable Run at startup, restart the PC, and observe that PowerToys does not start automatically.
The issue body and first comment include three PowerToysReport ZIP attachment links.
Automated triage initially said a bug report archive could not be safely analyzed because an oversized entry prevented diagnostic analysis.
The reporter replied: "OK, I added the report file."
The current labels include both Needs-Author-Feedback and Needs-Team-Response, indicating the author responded after a request for information.
No assignee, project item, or upstream PR is linked directly to issue 50379.
inferences: The latest author reply likely satisfies the generic request for a report ZIP, but the archive contents were not reanalyzed in this lightweight pass.
The symptom is not unique to this reporter; it matches the open startup tracker #23193 and a closed duplicate chain through #43395, #41683, and #36993.
The most likely owning code area is the runner/settings startup-task integration rather than an individual PowerToy module.
Because a broader open tracker already exists, a separate design action on 50379 would fragment duplicate reports and risk duplicated fix work.
issue_context.analysis: The report contains enough steps to recognize the failure family: the General page startup toggle persists to runner general settings, and the runner manages a per-user Task Scheduler logon task. Focused duplicate search found an open canonical tracker with the same behavior and several closed issues already routed into it. The maintainer action that best matches the public evidence is a duplicate-routing comment, not another request for generic logs and not a new fork-side design from this individual report.
initial_investigation: Read the full 50379 issue body, all three comments, labels, assignees, project items, and live updatedAt from GitHub.
Checked obvious duplicate chain: #43395 was closed as duplicate of #41683; #41683 was closed as duplicate of #36993; #36993 was closed as duplicate of open issue #23193.

Reviewed open #23193 and related #47161 summaries; #23193 remains open and contains multiple reports of PowerToys failing to run at startup while the setting is enabled, including administrator-mode cases.
Searched public upstream PRs for references to #50379, #43395, #41683, #36993, and #23193 and found no covering PR.

Inspected runner startup code: src/runner/general_settings.cpp applies the startup setting and calls create/delete_auto_start_task_for_this_user; src/runner/auto_start_helper.cpp creates a Task Scheduler logon task under the PowerToys folder with a three-second delay and optional highest run level.

Inspected Settings UI binding: src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/ViewModels/GeneralViewModel.cs maps the General page Startup toggle to GeneralSettingsConfig.Startup unless GPO controls it; GeneralPage.xaml exposes that toggle in Startup and permissions.

Inspected diagnostics ownership: tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/ReportGPOValues.cpp records the configured RunAtStartup GPO value, which would help distinguish policy disablement from task creation or launch failure.

Reviewed recent startup-task history: PR #48739 changed only the scheduled-task security descriptor to Local System, Administrators, and the task user, and stated no intended behavior change to startup or run-elevated flows.

comment.body: Thanks for adding the PowerToysReport ZIP. This looks like the same startup-task failure already tracked in #23193: Run at startup is enabled, PowerToys does not launch after reboot/logon, and prior similar reports (#43395 -> #41683 -> #36993) were consolidated into that open tracker. I think we should keep the investigation and diagnostics together there and close this as a duplicate of #23193 unless maintainers see a separate 0.101.2362-specific signal in the new report.
